transcription:
The newly formed Stevens Track and Field team joined several other schools partaking in the East Stroudsburg Invitational Championships in East Stroudsburg, Pennsylvania, Saturday March 15. This scrappy new team is manned with the strength of the Cross Country Club and newly found talent from the Stevens community.

Competition was under way as the starter's gun sounded for the sixty yard dash. Stevens was represented here by the "South American Dasher" himself, Tom Dasso. Dasso ('83) cracked the old school record of 7.28 seconds by one half of a second to squeak by the old record, clocking in at 7.20 seconds.

Moving on with the eight hours of events, the next event to be run by a Stevens man was the sixty yard high hurdles. Our own Mike "Skeets" Langmaid ('83), 8.70 seconds later, was to establish a new record, urged on by the cheers of his team and father. The quarter mile run followed and was run by former Penn Relay trackster Steve Lyons ('83). Steve set a new record for the distance, running 55.1 seconds. The fastest quarter mile in recent times by a Stevens man was set two years ago at the Rutgers Relays in the mile relay. This Stevens Olympic moment saw Keith Moore ('80) run the second leg of the mile relay in 53.4 seconds.

A one hour break preceded the commencement of the field events. Ernest Shiling ('82) straddled the shotput circle as he attempted to launch the 16 pound shotput. Mr. Bob Dynda ('83) followed thereafter, fortuitously establishing a new school record in the new event, tossing the little round ball 9.18 meters. The lack of any jumping events pushed off Roger Williams' ('83) chances of gracing the event with his imminent strides.

Moving right along, four members of the ever feared Cross Country squad embarked on the challenge of the distance medley. Sime Haas ('83) led off the race, running the half mile leg in a time of 2:07.53. The baton changed hands to senior Ian Howe. He took hold of the uncommon assignment of running the quarter mile and encircled the track in splits of 26.02 and 29.50 seconds, an ultimate 55.52 second quarter mile. The stick changed hands to Dave Arbeitel ('83), who kept the team in condition by running a fine 3/4 mile leg. Freshman sensation Albert Alonso ran the anchor leg, desperately attempting to capture first place. Plans took a turn when he became ill in the race, but he courageously finished the race, establishing a new school record in the process.

This particular relay team's efforts brought smiles to the entire team when the announcer of events listed the school's scores: Stevens had defeated the powerful Temple University.

The following events saw two runners take advantage of their versatile skills. Mike "Skeets" Langmaid posted a new school record in the 300 yard dash in a time of 38.94 seconds. This accomplishment was recorded by Mike, and possibly not by Louise Herrera, who was closing on a faster time when he slipped and fell 30 yards from the finish.

Angel Pineiro ('81) ran the final event. Angel ran a strong 880 yard run but will require development in several areas before he is to break Ian Howe's standing half mile record of 2:04.1 minutes, set last December at Lehigh University.

The team did very well overall in their amazing upset over Temple considering their limited conditioning. This spirited bunch of athletes are in the process of deeper development of their skills and will prove to be a dominant threat in this local region, as the very successful Cross Country squad proved to be. If you feel a yearning to express your track and field talents, drop a line in S-42.
summary: Recap of Stevens' debut as a newly formed Track and Field team at the East Stroudsburg Invitational, where multiple members set school records and the team scored an upset over Temple University.

First, on October 4 in New York at Van Cortlandt Park, Stevens defeated Hunter College 23-33, John Jay College 16-46, and N.Y. Poly 22-38 (lower score wins). Finishing first for Stevens was Al Alonso '83 in a school record 29:15 for the very hilly 5 mile course. In second was Dave Arbeitel in 30:57, followed by Maarten DeJong '84 in 31:21, Mike Browne '84 in 31:23, Atly Botas '84 in 32:37, Sime Haas in 33:15 and Juan Sanchez in 35:15.

On Wednesday, October 8, the Cross Country squad travelled to Ramapo College to face Ramapo and Medgar Evers. Without its number two runner, Dave Arbeitel, sidelined with the flu, the depth of this year's crew proved to be the major factor in the meet, as the team still easily defeated Ramapo 20-35 and Medgar Evers, who didn't have five runners finishing, thus automatically losing.

Undefeated in his first 5 races, Al Alonso again set a new Tech record for 10 kilometers in 33:36, followed by Maarten DeJong in 34:17, Mike Browne '84 in 34:30, Atly Botas in 37:05, Sime Haas in 37:28 and Ray Dion '84 in 40:15.

headline: X-C IAC Preview: Contenders
transcription:
Last weekend, due to the freshman finals, the team was forced to cancel its scheduled meet in N.Y. Our record is still (7-1), going into this Saturday's IAC Championship race at Drew University. This year's group of harriers is the strongest in Tech's history. The main competition for our squad will come from Drew and probably N.Y. Maritime, as well.

In accordance with this big event, the top 7 runners, and a list of their best performances to date, is as follows. Al Alonso '83 — our No. 1 runner all season, has broken school records on every course (Van Cortlandt Park 29:16). Dave Arbeitel '83 — Co-captain along with Alonso, has run consistently behind Al, though hampered by the flu; should be in top form due to his recent strong performances (Drew — 30:06). Wayne Sutton '83 — due to conflicts has until now been unable to race, but practicing on his own. He should finish high in the standings. Fernando DeLaVega '83 — our top runner last year. He has been hobbled by injuries all season, but has been training recently and hopefully will repeat his strong showing at last year's race. Mike Browne '84 — has been our 4th man to date and should continue to reach the top 5 (Van Cortlandt Park - 31:23). Atly Botas '84 — along with our other freshman harriers should be among the best in the IAC (Van Cortlandt - 32:37). Filling out the rest of the squad that we will be bringing to the IAC race are: Sime Haas '83, Juan Sanchez '83, John King '84, and Ray Dion '84. Our team, composed of all sophomores and freshmen, will be one of the contenders for the IAC crown and hopefully will be Stevens' first champion.

Also, last Sunday, freshman Maarten DeJong picked up 2 medals at the Secaucus Road race. Finishing second in the 2-mile run, in 10:36, he just missed the course record. In the 6-mile race, Maarten finished second in his age group, in 37:21. Congratulations.

headline: Coach Named
transcription:
Athletic Director "Buzz" Seymour announced that Bill Grothe will coach the cross country team this fall.

Grothe, who is the Director of Financial Aid at Stevens, thus becomes the first coach of the sport at the College. Students have been representing Tech on a club basis for the last several years. Cross country is now an intercollegiate varsity sport at Stevens.

Mr. Grothe first came to Stevens in 1979 after a four year period in the financial aid office at the University of Michigan. At the time he left that institution he was the Assistant Director for athletic and private scholarships.

He is a graduate of the University of Michigan, B.A., 1970, and obtained his Master of Social Work degree from that same university in 1973. Before returning to work in the financial aid office of his alma mater, he taught at the Methodist Children's Home in Redford Township, Michigan.

He is a native of Manchester, Michigan and currently lives in Plainsboro, N.J.
summary: Announces Bill Grothe, Stevens' Director of Financial Aid, as the first-ever coach of the newly varsity cross country program, with a short biography.

transcription:
On Saturday, Bill Grothe's cross country team makes their varsity debut at a quad meet against Pratt, Lehman and N.Y. Poly in Van Cortlandt Park in New York City. Cross country becomes the tenth active varsity sport at Tech, and Coach Grothe is looking forward to seeing each runner and the team improve and benefit from the experience.

The team has eleven members, six of whom are freshmen. Grothe feels that the junior tandem of Al Alonso of West New York and Dave Arbeitel of Clark will be the most consistent and strongest runners. Both Al and Dave were instrumental in cross country becoming a varsity sport. Each has two years of club experience at Stevens and outstanding high school backgrounds.

"We expect Al and Dave to lead the team in scoring," remarked Grothe.

Adding to the depth of the squad are freshmen of unusual promise, making the overall picture optimistic. headline: Sports Profile ... Al Alonso

transcription:
Al Alonso is a junior from West New York, and is Stevens' best hope of qualifying for the Nationals in the upcoming NCAA Division III Regionals at Lebanon Valley College in Pennsylvania next weekend. To do well will take an extraordinary effort, an effort that Al is certainly capable of.

In this very successful first season of varsity competition for the Stevens cross-country team (7 victories, 3 losses), Al has already broken his own Stevens record for the Van Cortlandt Park 5 mile course two times; the present record being 21:15. Al played an instrumental part in the founding of cross-country as a Stevens varsity sport, along with Dave Arbeitel. In addition, Al is President of the Stevens Tech Track and Field Club, while also studying Electrical Engineering. When asked to comment about his number one runner, first year coach Bill Grothe simply responded, "He loves to run", and added, "Al runs because he likes to win, a truly accomplished runner."

The league meet held at Drew showed what a true competitor Al really is. He competed in the race after suffering from a stomach virus and losing eight pounds during the three days preceding the meet. Al finished fourteenth, but with a time three minutes slower than he normally runs. However disappointing his showing might have been overall, the courage and competitive spirit that it took to run, much more to finish well up in the pack, was truly indicative of the exemplary attitude and ability of one of Stevens' finest athletes.

transcription:
With all of this year's squad returning, the future of the Cross Country team looks even brighter than its outstanding 7-3 initial season. Coach Grothe feels that Cross Country will grow into a strong program here at Stevens.

The coach noted that students are highly motivated people with self-discipline; this is the strength of the program at Stevens. These attributes are necessary for becoming a competitive runner. Mr. Grothe went on further to explain that the coach is looking forward to more women joining the program. This past season there was only one, Gina Delcasale, a junior. Miss Delcasale did have the opportunity to run against other women and enjoyed moderate success. "The women at Stevens," Mr. Grothe noted, "are as highly motivated and talented as the men. The addition of women to the team will enable them to compete more broadly."

Enjoying a fine season was junior Al Alonso. Always a competitor, he finished in the top five in each one of the dual meets. Al simply loves to run and holds the college record of 28:25 at Van Cortlandt Park, almost a minute and a half under his initial time there. A truly accomplished runner, Al simply likes to win.

Dave Arbeitel, also a junior, finished in the top seven in all of Tech's dual meets. His times showed much improvement as the season progressed, and he ran well at the regionals in Pennsylvania.

Showing considerable improvement during their tough freshman year were Manny Costa and Jeff Josephson. Manny, an extraordinary athlete, had solid times from the beginning of the season. The loss of Jeff (bronchitis) and Juan Sanchez (sprained ankle) during the league meet, along with Al being sick, might have cost a higher finish than third. This was without a doubt the most disappointing part of the season. Juan, the number four runner, contributed throughout the season and went to the Regionals held at Lebanon Valley College.

"The purpose of the team is to allow the students to enjoy what they like," Grothe remarked, "the team practices as a whole and always works together. Stevens is the right school for Cross Country; it has everything going for it." It is obvious both his coaching and his relationship with the students have a great deal going for them.

The cross-country team had a super day last Saturday at the Manhattanville Invitational. They beat all four of their dual meet opponents (NYU — 23 to 38, Lehman — 20 to 39, Manhattanville — 15 to 50, and Dominican — 15 to 50) raising their record to 7-2.

meet_or_event: Kings College Invitational; dual meet vs. N.J.I.T., Garrett Mountain
transcription:
By Michael Brigante

First some old news: two weeks ago, the Ducks raced at the Kings College Invitational, and based on last year's performance at the same event, the team looks like it has improved quite a bit. The best times for the entire field were significantly lower this year, but the Ducks still managed to do better than last year. This year we finished 11th out of twenty teams, an improvement over last year's 13th out of eighteen. Stevens' top five runners were Mike Tamkutonis (28:32), Greg Morriello (30:33), Mike Brigante (32:42), Jorge Rivera (33:21), and Bill Aramondo (33:54), with Cliff Smyth and Mike Wong close behind. This encouraging performance (all the veterans improved their previous times) got the team psyched for winning the meet against NJIT.

Last Saturday the Stevens Cross Country team earned its first win of the season when they defeated last year's IAC champions — NJIT. In a very close race at Garrett Mountain, Mike Tamkutonis led the Ducks with a time of 29:31, he was followed by two freshmen, Greg Morriello (32:11) and Cliff Smyth (33:57). Mike Brigante and Bill Aramondo rounded out Stevens' top 5 runners, but equally important were Jorge Rivera and Mike Wong, who ran hard to push back NJIT's fourth man enough to allow a win for the Ducks. The final score was 28-31. Jack Lee, the newest member of the team, had an impressive showing for his first race, and took 12th place overall. Coach Al Alonso didn't seem very impressed by the win, and said "we still have a lot of work to do," referring to preparing for the IAC championships, for which every member of the team will have to improve their times in order to win. The team is looking forward to a hopefully undefeated season, and will be racing again this Sunday at Van Cortlandt Park in New York.
summary: Recapping an improved 11th-place finish at Kings College and Stevens' first win of the season over defending IAC champion N.J.I.T.
notability_note: First win of the season, over the defending IAC champion, N.J.I.T.

headline: Cross Country 3-1 Record
meet_or_event: Meet at Van Cortlandt Park vs. John Jay College, CCNY, and NYU
transcription:
The cross country team had a successful outing at Van Cortland Park, Sunday, and came home with a pair of wins. Junior Mike Tamkutonis placed first for Stevens at 29:49, about two minutes faster than his previous time at the course last season. Freshman Greg Morriello came in next with a 31:44 clocking. Mike Wong, a senior, followed at 34:00. Finishing fourth and fifth, respectively, for the team, were senior Jorge Rivera and Chick Li, a freshman. Rivera was timed at 34:19, Li came in at 36:01. Coach Alonso felt Li's performance was crucial in the victories.

Cross Country 3-1 Record

By Jorge Rivera, Box S-1090

Two weeks ago Stevens defeated last year's IAC champs, NJIT. Our runners continue to advance, improving the record last Sunday. The City College of NY (CCNY) hosted a meet at Van Cortland Park in the Bronx. Stevens topped John Jay College and CCNY, but lost to a strong NYU team. We overcame injuries to key runners on Sunday, but we expect them back for our meet this weekend. Out of a field of 24 runners, Mike Tamkutonis led the Ducks, placing 6th with a five-mile time of 29:49 min. His previous best for the course was 31:38 min. Hopefully, the next time we run at Van Cortland he will break the school record. Freshman Greg Morriello placed 10th with 31:44. Mike Wong came in next for Stevens with 34:00 min., improving his time for this course by 1:24 min. Jorge Rivera was the fifth man at 34:19, also improving his course time by 1:45 min. Freshman Jack Lee continues to do well with a time of 36:01. Good work everyone!
summary: Stevens went 2-1 at a Van Cortlandt Park meet, beating John Jay and CCNY but losing to NYU, improving the season record to 3-1.

meet_or_event: IAC regional meet, Garrett Mountain; Bard College Invitational
transcription:
[Opening lines cut off from a preceding article.] ...as usual did well at 28:07, although as a team we did not fare well. Congratulations to Mike Wong, who did his best time on any course at 31:41. The season will be coming to an end soon. The last remaining meets are the Ramapo Invitational tomorrow and a meet against Yeshiva and Pratt on November 13th.

Cross-Country: 2nd In [conference — headline partly cut off]

By Jorge Rivera, Box S-1090

On Wednesday October 19th the IAC regional meet was held at Garrett Mountain in Paterson. We were hoping to upset last year's champs, NJIT, like we had done in a dual meet against them. We easily topped the other schools in our conference: NY Maritime, NY Polytechnic Institute, and the College of Mt. St. Vincent. But, we lost the title to NJIT, despite some fine performances. Mike Tamkutonis placed second and broke his own 5-mile course record with a time of 29:13 min. Greg Morriello, Mike Wong, and Jorge Rivera also saved their best for the tough IAC course. Each improved their best time for the course. Cliff Smyth came back from injuries to do well also.

This past Saturday we went to the Bard College Invitational. After a 2½ hour ride to upstate NY we found that very few teams decided to come and brave the weather. Our Stevens team did brave the rain and thick mud to place second. One downhill was so treacherous that we had to practically walk down to avoid falling flat on our faces. Ironically, accustomed as we are to bad conditions, few of us brought a change of clothes. We resorted to using the hand dryer in the locker room to dry off clothes. I won't mention any names, but I will say that Mike Tamkutonis, Greg Morriello, Mike Wong, Jorge Rivera, Cliff Smyth, and our manager [name illegible] were the lucky ones.
summary: Stevens finished second (of four IAC teams) to N.J.I.T. at the conference championship, with Mike Tamkutonis breaking his own course record, then placed second at a muddy Bard College Invitational.

headline: Track and Field Club
transcription:
By Mike Tamkutonis, S-1090

The Track and Field team will be active again this semester. We have six meets scheduled in April and a road race in March. Our meets and practices are on different days of the week to accommodate your schedule.

If you are interested in joining, please try to attend our first meeting. It will be on Wed., Feb. 15th at 3:30 p.m. Meet us by the bulletin board in Walker Gym. Bring a copy of your class schedule and be prompt because we will have a club picture taken.

We expect to be very competitive this year. The schools we will be competing against are also on a club level. For instance, at last year's William Paterson meet we placed in several events. This year we will return with a bigger and better trained people.

We are also ambitious enough to attempt to host an informal meet against NJIT and Mt. St. Vincent College at the newly renovated track in North Bergen. The track is only 20 minutes away from Hoboken by car. With the enthusiastic help of Mr. Frisco and Mr. Nast of the Stevens administration, we should have the necessary insurance coverage that North Bergen township requires.

Watch the Stute for further announcements, especially concerning events like the long jump, shot put, hurdles, discus and javelin. If you can't make the meeting, contact Jorge at Box S-1090 for more information.
summary: Announces the Track and Field Club's spring 1989 season, an organizational meeting, and a plan to host a home meet at a newly renovated North Bergen track.

headline: Track and Field Club: 1-0
meet_or_event: Meet vs. College of Mount Saint Vincent, Hudson County Park, North Bergen
transcription:
By Jorge Rivera

The Track and Field Club won its first home meet ever on Wednesday, April 5, 1989. We competed against the College of Mount Saint Vincent. The meet was held at Hudson County Park in North Bergen, NJ, which is only 30 minutes north of Stevens. The town renovated their track only last year so it was very good. The only hitch was that the town requires insurance coverage. I'm grateful to the Administration for helping us out enthusiastically. We should be able to repeat the meet next year.

Mike Acquah was the hot runner on Wednesday. He won the 100m and 200m with great times of 10.84 sec. and 23.14 sec. respectively. Mike Bradford helped the team's depth in the sprinting events by taking fourth in the 100m with a time of 11.80 sec.; hope we can put a good sprint relay team together with them in it.

We're also proud of Greg Morriello and Bill Aromando. They threw the discus, taking first and second with 77'5" and 74'9¼" respectively. In the shot put, Bill took second place and Greg third with throws of 24'11½" and 24'9½". They also ran, with Greg placing second in the 800m with a time of 2:26 min and Bill running the 200m. Our top runner from cross-country, Mike Tamkutonis, finished first in the 1600m with 5:16 min.

Track and Field covers all events possible. On Wednesday, we had the 400m, 200m, 400m, 800m, 1600m, discus, shotput and javelin, which was rained out. We did not hold other events because the other school did not have enough athletes to cover the events. Our team is basically a men's team. However, the College of Mount Saint Vincent's had a women's team too. Thanks go to Danielle Cordani, who ran the 100m. She was our only girl competing.

The times and distances shown here are typical of track meets we compete at. Stevens and other teams fight the poor weather from January to March as well as the busy schedules of the students. Our club is geared toward allowing flexibility, while remaining reasonably competitive given these constraints.

If you would like to see a typical meet, you may attend our last meet at William Paterson College even if you're not in great shape. Meet us in front of the Walker Gym at 2:45 - 3:00 pm on Wed., April 19. We should be back by 6:30 p.m. Two other meets will be held by the time you read this, which will be reported soon.
summary: The Track and Field Club won its first-ever home meet against the College of Mount Saint Vincent at a newly renovated North Bergen track, with strong performances from Mike Acquah and Greg Morriello.
notability_note: Club's first home meet win in its history.

headline: Cross Country is Off and Running
transcription:
Cross Country is Off and Running

The Stevens Cross-Country Team started off its season last Saturday in the rain at the Wagner Invitational. This is the first time the team has competed in the invitational in several years.

The first five finishers for the Ducks were (in order) co-captain and senior Mike Tamkutonis, freshman Chris Houghton, sophomore Lou Coless, co-captain and sophomore Greg Moriello, and Bill Aromondo, who all managed to see the course without getting lost in the fog on their glasses. Mike had an impressive run of 29:45 for the five mile course.

Overall, the Ducks finished 11th out of nineteen teams in the meet, a highly competitive event. Coach Al Alonso believes that the team is very strong this year (the team currently consists of ten members) and has a good shot at the IAC Championships. The Duck's next meet is at the KEAN Invitational this coming Saturday.

A note to those who signed up for the team on activities night: we'd like to see you at practice Wednesday at 3 pm, and Saturday and Sunday at 9 am in the Walker Gym. If you're interested and didn't sign up, drop by anyway!
summary: Stevens opened the 1989 season with an 11th-place finish at the Wagner Invitational, its first appearance there in several years, led by co-captain Mike Tamkutonis.

headline: Cross Country
transcription:
Cross Country

For all you loyal fans who faithfully showed up to cheer on your favorite cross-country team last Saturday at Kean College, NJ, we're sorry. The meet was at King's College, NY.

The Ducks, apparently starting a new tradition of racing in the rain, finished ninth out of 20 teams. Our top five finishers in order were Mike Tamkutonis, Chris Houghton, Lou Coless, Greg Morriello, and Bill Aromando (who saved it all for the last 100 meters just to sprint it in for all those girls at the finish line). Asked for a quote, Coach Al Alonso said, "Well, don't quote me on this, but we should win the IAC Championships. On the other hand, I'm very happy with how the team ran, everybody improved except for Lou, and Cliff did not finish last." Lou must hand back his Budweiser Athlete of the Week certificate and will not get his complementary keg.

Our next meet is this coming Saturday at 11:00 at Garret Mountain against our arch rival, NJIT, if they even show up, if in fact they even have a team.
summary: Stevens finished ninth of 20 teams at the King's College Invitational, with Coach Al Alonso predicting the team would win the IAC Championships.

headline: Cross Country
meet_or_event: Meet at Van Cortlandt Park vs. John Jay, CCNY, Mount Saint Vincent, and NYU
transcription:
Cross Country

The Stevens Cross Country Team put in a strong performance at Van Cortlandt Park, N.Y. last Saturday, defeating John Jay, CCNY, and Mount Saint Vincent College, and losing only to NYU. The Ducks beat John Jay 38-19, CCNY 34-25, and edged out MSV 29-28.

Our 6th and 7th runners, Cliff Smyth and Steve Kostakis, were crucial to our win over MSV. They displaced MSV's fifth runner by two places, which was just enough for our victory.

The top five finishers for our team were Mike Tamkutonis, 29:51; Chris Houghton, 31:42; Lou Coless, 32:04; Gregg Morriello, 32:20; and Chik Li, 34:52, at the most popular course on the east coast. Our next meet is the Drew Invitational this Saturday at 11:00.
summary: Stevens went 3-1 in a four-team meet at Van Cortlandt Park, edging Mount Saint Vincent by one point thanks to its depth runners.

headline: Cross Country
transcription:
Cross Country

The Stevens cross-country team had a few problems at their last meet, the Drew Invitational. First, our top runner and co-captain Mike Tamkutonis couldn't be there because of the GRE's. Then team members Bill Aromando, Chris Houghton, Jack Li, and Mike Brigante were nowhere to be found. To top it all off, Cliff Smyth made the poor choice of following two Drew runners in the late stages of the race who took a wrong turn and led him two miles away from the finish line.

Something positive did happen, though. Greg Moriello finished first for the Ducks, setting a Stevens record (31:30) for the 5-mile course. Lou Coless and Steven Kostakis finished second and third for the Ducks.

The Ducks intend to finish off the season with a bang, running the Ramapo Invitational on Saturday, and against Yeshiva and Polytechnic at Van Cortlandt Park on Sunday. And of course, the IAC Championship is next Wednesday.
summary: A chaotic Drew Invitational saw several Stevens runners absent or lost on course, but Greg Moriello set a new Stevens 5-mile course record.
notability_note: Greg Moriello set a new Stevens 5-mile course record (31:30) at the Drew Invitational.

headline: Cross Country
meet_or_event: Ramapo Invitational; dual meet vs. Yeshiva and Polytechnic
transcription:
Cross Country

The Stevens Cross Country Team fared well at the Ramapo Invitational on Saturday. The Ducks picked up a trophy for their third place team finish. Mike Tamkutonis finished seventh overall. He and Bill Aramondo picked up a shirt for finishing in the top fifteen. The top finishers for Stevens were Mike, Bill, Lou Coless, Jack Li, and Steve Kosakis. As an interesting note, Mike Tamkutonis beat the time of Coach Al Alonso, who also ran in the race.

On Sunday, Stevens edged out Yeshiva 28-27 at Van Cortlandt Park. Polytechnic was a no-show (wimps!). With the victory, the team increased its record to 4 and 1.

The top 5 runners in this race for the Ducks were Mike Tamkutonis, Greg Moriello, Chris Houghton, Lou Coless, and Jack Li.
summary: Stevens took third at the Ramapo Invitational and edged Yeshiva by one point in a dual meet, improving to 4-1 on the season.

headline: Stevens Cross-Country Team — IAC CHAMPS!!!
transcription:
Stevens Cross-Country Team — IAC CHAMPS!!!

The Stevens Cross Country Team finished up a sensational season by winning the IAC Championships at Garrett Mountain Park last Wednesday. Participating in the meet were Yeshiva, Polytechnic, Mount St. Vincent, and Maritime. Coach Al Alonso said of the win, "I'm very pleased, the entire team put in its best performance of the year for this race and it paid off."

Stevens claimed three of the five medals awarded to the top five finishers of the race. Senior and co-captain Mike Tamkutonis took the first place medal with a time of 29:23. Co-captain Greg Moriello nabbed the fourth place medal with his time of 30:25, and Chris Houghton won fifth place with a time of 30:42. Fourth [sic] for Tech was Lou Coless, 31:50, and fifth, Cliff Smyth with 33:02.

The Cross-country team wants to give a big "Thank You" to the team manager, Angie Roda, for her devoted efforts. Also a big congratulations to Mike T. for finishing first for the Ducks every meet he ran.

The team appears to be in great shape for next year, with Sophomores Greg Moriello, Lou Coless, Cliff Smyth, Jack Li and Steve Kostakis in better shape than ever. Freshman Chris Houghton plans to run 27's next year. The Ducks plan on keeping the title next year, and the Stute wishes them every success in doing so.
summary: Stevens Cross Country capped a sensational season by winning the IAC Championship at Garrett Mountain, led by individual champion Mike Tamkutonis.
notability_note: IAC Cross Country Championship win — the program's second title, after 1982 — led by Mike Tamkutonis's individual first-place finish.
